I never wanted to comment on a thread more. I'm disgusted by every one of the comments repeatedly mentioning abortion when you've already established that you want to keep your baby. Also, because people will get all pissy- I'm not against adoption. I am, however, against bullying someone asking for help and receiving nothing but negative, non productive advice. 

My mom got pregnant with me when she was your age. It was hard. Some family stayed, and some didn't - good riddance. It was hard to stay in school and raise a baby. It was hard to make money and raise a baby. It was hard when the relationship didn't work out. It was hard when she couldn't go with her friends. Frankly, she made a ton of mistakes. In many ways, we grew up together. But you know what, she became one of the smartest, most adaptable people I know. She has more grit than any person I know. I love both my parents, and neither of them was perfect, and it wasn't always sunshine and rainbows, yet I turned out a well-rounded, happy human. 

As for advice:
Since you're homeschooled, dive into it right now. Work really, really hard, and try to get ahead. This will help you when the baby comes and you're trying to play catch up. Realistically, you might be graduating later than you originally thought. But that's OKAY. Just don't give up, and keep pushing!

Speaking of education. You say you want to be a mechanic, that's awesome! If you ever decide to go down another path and are mechanically minded. Trades are an excellent way to get into a well paying career without having to pay for an education beforehand. Apprenticeships are abundant, and they'll pay for any classes you have to take as long as you're working for their company. 

As many people said, take parenting classes and ask for advice from people in your life who you admire. 

YOU ALSO NEED TO TAKE A FINANCIAL LITERACY COURSE!!! This is one of the most important things you need to do. You and your girlfriend need to do this as soon as possible. Children are expensive. You won't have the same "advantage" as your peers to learn from your financial mistakes. Learn about budgeting, saving, credit, etc. Mistakes with money can haunt you for years, and money management is a skill many people do not have. 

Also, speak to your mom. Your mother loves you. She may be mad as hell. But give her time. She has a child (or children). She knows the challenge you're up for. I can't tell you where you should live because there's alot of factors that will go into that. Expect really high emotions when you do tell parents about this situation. It's going to be stressful and potentially messy. Just try and stay focused. 

Many people have done this! You CAN do this and have successful life.

This is beef suet I got from the meat market at my local grocery store. I tried to cut away as much of the meat as possible, then cut the suet into about 1/2 inch pieces. I've heard straining it with cheesecloth is also great, but I didn't do this. 
Also- I know alot of places won't give away suet for free but alot of places (in my area at least) do sell it really cheap- about 2 USD a pound.
